battle.name: 沌口之戰
battle.brief: 公元567年（北魏神龜三年、陳光大元年），北魏大將楊大眼率二十萬眾南伐，陳朝宿將侯瑱率湘州兵北援，戰於長江與漢水交會的沌口，陳軍大破魏軍，斬首數萬級，魏軍北退。卡面的羅馬弩砲屬公元前一世紀的扭力器械，與本役相隔六百餘年，其「一發一矢」的原理在同期中國以床弩、弩車延續。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 這場戰爭是南北朝後期北魏對南朝梁（陳）的正面軍事攻勢，發生於公元567年，即北魏神龜三年、南朝陳光大元年。南方的政權在557年由陳霸先建立、以梁的舊疆域為基礎的陳朝，但史籍仍常以「梁」稱之，故此役亦有「梁魏沌口之戰」的說法。北方一方的北魏此時由宣武帝拓跋宏在位，軍國大政由樞密與諸將分掌，籍貫河朔的宿將楊大眼為南征主將；南方一方的陳朝由陳蒨的弟弟陳伯即位，湘州一系的宿將侯瑱奉詔率師北援荊州，與侯安都、熊曇生、張彪等同鄉將領同行。戰役的地理框架是江淮與江漢兩條水道：魏軍自襄陽沿漢水南下，陳軍由湘州溯江而北，兩軍在長江與漢水交會的沌口相遇。交戰雙方都不是以全境兵力和單一戰場決勝負：北方以騎兵與河運補給壓境，南方以水網、城防與弩陣守禦。這一役因此是北方騎兵第一次在漢水下游被南朝以水障與集中弩射擊退的戰役。
countriesEn: This war was a full-scale southern offensive by Northern Wei against the southern court of Liang, by then the Chen, fought in 567 CE, the third year of the Northern Wei era Shengshen and the first year of the Chen era Guangda. The southern regime was the dynasty Chen Baxian had founded in 557 on the territory Liang had left behind, but the transmitted histories still habitually call it Liang, which is why this clash is also known as the battle of Dunkou between Liang and Wei. On the northern side Northern Wei was ruled by Emperor Xuanwu, Tuoba Hong, with the military affairs of the state divided among the central secretariat and a body of seasoned generals, the spearhead of the invasion being Yang Dayan, a veteran of long standing from the northern river lands; on the southern side the Chen court was held by Chen Bo, the younger brother of the late Emperor Wen, and the old general of the Xiangzhou school, Hou Zhen, was ordered to march north with reinforcements for Jingzhou, accompanied by fellow Xiangzhou commanders such as Hou Andu, Xiong Tan Sheng and Zhang Biao. The geographical frame of the campaign was formed by the two water routes of the Jiang and the Huai: the Wei army came down the Han from Xiangyang, while the Chen army pushed north along the Xiang, and the two met at Dunkou, where the Yangtze and the Han join. Neither side was committing its whole realm or settling the matter in a single field: the north pressed in with cavalry and river-borne supply, the south defended with a net of waterways, city works and crossbow volleys. The battle was therefore the first time a northern cavalry force was thrown back in the lower Han valley by the southern court using water barriers and massed crossbow fire.
people: 決定戰局的是湘州宿將侯瑱（字叔玉，衡陽人）。他在侯景之亂中自湘州起兵討伐，憑驍勇與熟悉山林水道逐步坐鎮荊湘，陳朝建立後成為中南一線最能倚重的支柱；此次北魏大舉南侵，他以高齡臨危受命，率湘州精兵北上，選擇在沌口這一段江漢之交的水域接敵。北方主將楊大眼是北魏中期最能打的將領之一，少一目而勇猛善射，早年在西域與涼州屢建功業，505至507年間曾隨魏主南征，受挫於梁將韋叡、曹景宗之手，褒斜道石門的《楊大眼造像記》正是那一役前後留下的題刻。時隔六十年，他再度率大軍南下，志在重演鍾離的功業，不料在沌口遇上與鍾離完全不同的地形，被侯瑱以弩陣與水障破了騎兵銳氣。南朝方面的關鍵人物還有侯安都、熊曇生、張彪等侯瑱同鄉，都是湘州軍的柱石；侯瑱在戰後不久因病薨於軍中，湘州軍系一時失去重心，其子侯景又因驕縱不法被誅，這一系此後再未恢復元氣。北魏宣武帝拓跋宏在肅清權臣高肇之後把國策轉向南方，陳朝皇帝陳伯年幼、諸王爭端未息，兩朝內部的處境同樣決定了這場戰役的走向。
peopleEn: The man who decided the outcome was Hou Zhen, courtesy name Shuyu, a native of Hengyang in Xiangzhou. He had raised troops in Xiangzhou against Hou Jing during the Hou Jing rebellion and, by his daring and his knowledge of the wooded country and the waterways of the middle Yangtze, had built up a power base in Jing and Xiang that the new Chen court leaned on as its most reliable pillar in the central south; when the north moved in strength he accepted command despite his age and led the pick of the Xiangzhou troops north, choosing to meet the enemy in the stretch of water where the Han and the Yangtze meet. The northern commander was Yang Dayan, one of the most capable generals of middle Northern Wei, one-eyed but fearless and a fine shot, who had made his name in the western regions and in Liangzhou and who had campaigned south with the Wei emperor between 505 and 507, where he was checked at Zhongli by the Liang generals Wei Rui and Cao Jingzong; the inscription carving the Yang Dayan image in the stone gate of the Baoxi road is the epigraphic trace left by roughly that campaign. Sixty years on he came south again with a great army, hoping to repeat the performance of Zhongli, and instead found at Dunkou a terrain entirely unlike Zhongli, where his cavalry were broken by a crossbow line and a barrier of water. The other southern figures of the hour were Hou Andu, Xiong Tan Sheng and Zhang Biao, all from the same Xiangzhou school and all pillars of its army; Hou Zhen fell ill soon after the battle and died in the field, and the Xiangzhou military group lost its centre of gravity, while his son Hou Jing was later executed for arrogance and misconduct, so that the group never recovered its strength. On the northern side Emperor Xuanwu of Wei, having cleared away the regent Gao Zhao, turned the policy of the state southward; and in the Chen the child emperor Chen Bo and the mutual suspicion of the princes and great ministers showed that the internal condition of both courts shaped this war as much as the armies did.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬弩砲（Scorpio）造於公元前一世紀：木製機身，扭力簧束儲能，一具機括發射一具重箭，羅馬人用它拆掉希臘城牆、也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。它與567年的沌口之戰相隔約六百一十年，不可能在戰場上出現，但它所代表的技術類別在同期中國有對應物：就是靠人力或絞盤蓄力、把單支重箭射出去的弩砲一類器械，在南北朝稱作床弩、弩車，一發一矢的形制與羅馬弩砲幾乎同構。中國方面更早就有同類的拋射器械，曹操與曹丕在官渡、襄樊、漢中一役用發石車破雲梯，正與羅馬將軍維吉烏斯記載的扭力弩砲同一技術世代；而梁、魏在江淮攻防中真正倚賴的攻城器械是撞車、雲梯、火箭與填隙用的布袋，守城一方則以櫓、突火椎、拒馬與壘塞應對。北魏的裝備以騎兵為骨幹：披札甲、控弦而射，配長刀與槊，攻城時另備偏廂車與運糧用的木鵝，即以土袋裝糧浮渡淮水的一種運載辦法，水軍靠舟船與檣檝，糧秣自襄陽沿漢水北岸轉運。南朝陳軍的骨幹是弩兵與步兵：弓弩兼施，強弩與床弩壓制城頭與河道，近身用環首刀、鐵鏨、槊，守城披兜鍪、鍑鍔，水師有船與竹排，糧秣走湘江與長江的水運。漢水兩岸的兵裝、舟車與糧道，才是這一役真正決定勝負的器械體系。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman Scorpio, made in the first century BC: a wooden frame storing energy in a skein of twisted sinew, one machine throwing one heavy bolt, the instrument with which the Romans pulled down Greek walls and with them the Greek system of city states. It stands some six hundred and ten years away from the battle of Dunkou in 567 and cannot have been present on the field, but the technological family it represents does have a Chinese counterpart in the same period: engines that stored power by manpower or windlass and then threw a single heavy bolt, called bed crossbows or bolt-throwers in the Southern and Northern Dynasties, a one-bolt-per-shot form almost identical in principle to the Roman scorpio. China had possessed such traction artillery even earlier, and Cao Cao and Cao Pi used stone-throwers to break the siege ladders of the enemy at Guandu, Xiangfan and Hanzhong, in the same technological generation as the torsion bolt-throwers described by the Roman general Vegetius; what the Liang and the Wei actually relied on in the campaigns across the Jiang and the Huai were rams, scaling ladders, fire-arrows and sacks of earth used to fill the gaps in a wall, while the defenders answered with mantlets, fire-poles, caltrops and ditches filled with stakes. The backbone of the Northern Wei army was cavalry: men in lamellar armour shooting from the saddle, with long sabres and spears, and for the siege, carts drawn up in echelon and the wooden goose, a floating bag of earth and grain used to ferry provisions across the Huai. Their naval strength was boats and light skiffs, and their grain came up the north bank of the Han from Xiangyang. The backbone of the southern Chen army was the crossbowmen and the foot: bows and crossbows used together, heavy crossbows and bed crossbows covering the walls and the river, the short weapons of the close fight being ring-pommel sabres, iron maces and spears, while the defenders wore iron helmets and plated armour, and the river force had boats and bamboo rafts moving their grain by the Xiang and the Yangtze. The armour, the boats and the supply lines of the two banks of the Han were the real instrument system that settled this battle.
tactics: 北魏軍的推進路線是沿水路向南的梯次行軍：先鋒騎兵自襄陽出發，循漢水北岸疾行，搜索並清除沿途據點；中軍帶著撞車、雲梯與糧車，緩行於後；殿後護著運糧的木鵝與輜重。漢水在此處寬闊多汊，水位隨季節漲落，冬季水淺則舟行吃水不足，騎兵可以涉水而舟師不能，遂令魏軍的攻勢與糧秣拉開距離；這種分進合擊的部署在平坦的淮北原野是長處，一旦河道交錯、蘆葦叢生便成了累贅，隊形被水分割，騎兵的衝鋒速度無法疊加。陳軍的應對是典型的以水制騎：侯瑱不與魏軍爭原野，而是把主力壓在江夏至沌口一線的南岸與水面上，舟師先占江面並封住漢水下游的渡口，步兵在岸上架弩，強弩與床弩在堤岸、洲渚與城頭居高臨下覆蓋河道，魏軍先鋒一旦進入弩的射界便遭密集箭矢打散，隊形一亂，陳軍的騎兵與步卒再由兩側夾擊，掩護魏軍退卻時的混亂追擊。守城與野戰的配合同樣關鍵：陳方以短兵與櫓結陣抵擋登城與衝突，把魏軍拖在城垣與水障之間，使其既不能展開騎兵，也不能展開攻城器械；反過來，魏軍若不能迅速拿下城池、不能在糧秣斷絕前取勝，久戰對它不利。全役的勝負節奏因此決定在兩點上：弩陣能把魏軍先鋒打成什麼樣子，以及陳軍自己的後方能撐多久。
tacticsEn: The Wei advance was a laddered march southward along the water: the vanguard cavalry set out from Xiangyang and moved quickly along the north bank of the Han, clearing the strongholds on the way; the centre followed more slowly with the rams, the ladders and the baggage carts; the rear guarded the grain and the trains, including the wooden geese that carried it. The Han is wide and braided in this stretch and its level rises and falls with the season, so in winter the shallow water let the cavalry ford where the boats could not move, which pulled the Wei offensive apart from its own supply; that pattern of advance in separate columns was an advantage on the open plains north of the Huai, but in a country of crossing channels and reed beds it became a burden, the formation cut up by the water and the speed of the cavalry charge impossible to add up. The Chen answer was the classic way of using water against horsemen: Hou Zhen did not contest the open country but pressed his main body against the south bank and the water surface from Jiangxia to Dunkou, the flotilla taking the river first and closing the crossings below the Han, the foot soldiers setting up their crossbows on the bank, heavy and bed crossbows on the levees, the islets and the walls looking down on the channel, so that the Wei vanguard, once inside the range, was broken by the weight of arrows, and the formation it lost was then finished off by the Chen horse and foot closing from both sides and cutting up the retreat. The combination of field and siege defence mattered as much: the Chen held short weapons and mantlets in a tight line to meet the assault and the clash, tying the Wei down between walls and water so that it could deploy neither its cavalry nor its siege engines; conversely the Wei could not afford a long war, since it could not take the city quickly and could not win before its grain ran out. The rhythm of the whole engagement therefore turned on two things: what the crossbow line did to the Wei vanguard, and how long the Chen rear could hold.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰役在公元567年，即北魏神龜三年、南朝陳光大元年；交戰月份史籍未明確記載，卡面標為正月，取的是天嘉六年冬北魏大舉出兵、次年春天接戰的推算。北方投入的兵力，《梁書》與《陳書》一系記為「眾二十萬」，這是史家沿用的誇大數目，實際投入戰鬥的當然遠少於此，可信的是魏軍兵馬相當充足、並以騎兵為前導；南方以侯瑱所部湘州兵為主力，另有江夏、武昌一線的守軍配合，總數沒有留下記載。距離上，魏軍自襄陽順漢水南下至沌口約六百里，前段尚在魏境，後段全在敵後河川地帶；糧秣自襄陽分批北運，木鵝運糧一次可載的量極有限，補給線一旦被截斷，前線撐不過數日。戰果方面，兩《書》均記陳軍「斬首數萬級」，並記魏軍退回；此役之後，侯瑱因舊疾發作、病勢加重，於同年薨於軍中，時年五十七，朝廷為他舉行哀禮，追贈太尉，諡曰昭毅。他的同鄉將領侯安都、熊曇生、張彪則繼續領兵，成為陳朝在江漢與江淮一線的依靠。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are roughly these. The battle was fought in 567 CE, the third year of the Northern Wei era Shengshen and the first year of the Chen era Guangda; the month of the engagement is not clearly recorded in the transmitted histories, and the card gives January, following the reckoning that the Wei invasion was launched in the winter of the sixth year of Tianjia and joined in the spring of the following year. The northern force is recorded in the Liang shu and the Chen shu as twenty myriads of men, the usual exaggeration of the historians; what can be believed is that the Wei army was amply supplied with men and horses and led with cavalry. The south fought with the Xiangzhou troops of Hou Zhen as its main body, with the garrisons of Jiangxia and Wuchang cooperating; no total survives. In distance, the Wei marched from Xiangyang down the Han for some six hundred li, the first part still in Wei territory and the whole of the later part through river country behind the enemy lines. Grain moved north from Xiangyang in batches, and a wooden goose could carry very little on one trip, so that once the supply line was cut the front could hold for only a few days. As for results, both histories record that the Chen cut off tens of thousands of heads and that the Wei fell back; after the battle Hou Zhen's old complaint worsened, his illness grew heavier, and he died in the field in the same year at the age of fifty-seven, the court mourning him and granting him the posthumous title of Grand Commander, with the name Zhaoyi. His fellow townsmen Hou Andu, Xiong Tan Sheng and Zhang Biao went on to command troops and became the Chen's reliance on the Jinghan and Jianghuai lines.
cause: 北魏在神龜年間把國策轉向南方，是有清楚的國內背景的。宣武帝拓跋宏在515年之後肅清以高肇為首的權臣，攬回了被分割的兵權；此後他連續對江淮用兵，企圖把北魏的統治線從河南推到淮水以南，進而圖謀荊州。梁末侯景之亂使南朝元氣大傷，士卒耗散、府庫空虛，荊州的防務尤其殘破，襄樊一線的城鎮多已殘破難守；557年陳霸先建立陳朝，四境雖粗定，朝廷內部仍暗潮洶湧，陳蒨在566年去世後，繼位的陳伯年少，諸王與重臣互相猜疑，調兵與糧餉的效率遠不如戰前。北方看準的正是這個空隙：南朝內部更替的年份、荊州守軍的空缺、襄陽到江夏之間水道上的薄弱環節，都被計算在這一輪南征的計畫裡。陳朝並非沒有警覺，荊州方面連續發警，朝廷才把湘州的兵馬交給侯瑱率領北上——這支兵是他十多年來在侯景之亂中親手帶出來的老底子，是陳朝中南戰區最後一支可以信賴的機動兵力，兵不血刃地用於救援，本身就說明陳朝在江淮與荊襄的縱深已經不夠。
causeEn: The turn of Northern Wei's policy toward the south in the years of the Shengshen era had a clear background at home. Emperor Xuanwu, Tuoba Hong, had cleared out the regent Gao Zhao and the men around him after 515 and took back a military authority that had been split apart; from then on he campaigned against the Jiang and the Huai year after year, trying to push the line of Wei rule from Henan south of the Huai and thence toward Jingzhou. The Hou Jing rebellion had left the southern court drained, the soldiers scattered and the treasuries empty, and the defences of Jingzhou were in a particularly ruined state, many towns between Xiangyang and Jiangnan having been battered and left unkeepable. When Chen Baxian founded the Chen in 557 the realm was only roughly settled and dark currents ran under the surface of the court; after Chen Qian died in 566 the young Chen Bo succeeded him, and the princes and the great ministers watched one another, so that the speed with which troops and provisions could be moved was nothing like what it had been. The north had measured exactly this gap: the years of southern succession, the empty garrisons of Jingzhou, the weak points of the water route between Xiangyang and Jiangxia were all entered into the plan of that offensive. The Chen were not without warning, for Jingzhou raised the alarm repeatedly, and only then did the court hand the Xiangzhou army to Hou Zhen to march north; those were the old soldiers he had raised himself during the Hou Jing rebellion, the last body of mobile troops in the central south on which the Chen could rely, and committing them without a battle is itself a sign that the depth of the Chen in the Jianghuai and Jingxiang lines was no longer sufficient.
impact: 這一仗的意義不在於斬獲多少，而在於它標出了一條北魏南進的極限線。沌口之戰之後，漢水下游仍然是陳朝的防區，襄陽以下的荊北屏障沒有被突破；直到隋文帝開皇九年589年隋軍渡江滅陳，中原王朝要重新拿下江漢與江淮，仍然要沿著襄陽、江夏、建康這條線由西向東推。也就是說，567年之後的九百多年裡，這段水道反覆成為南北攻防的分界線，侯瑱在沌口守住的位置，正是後來隋軍花費最大力氣才突破的同一道關口。對陳朝而言，勝仗的代價卻由個人承擔：最能打的宿將一死，湘州軍系元氣大傷，侯瑱的兒子侯景又因驕縱被誅，這個集團此後再未出現像侯瑱這樣能獨當一面的人物，江北防務的重擔落回朝廷與荊州將領身上，幾年之後侯景之亂式的內部崩潰在陳朝末年再度上演，只是換了主角。對北魏而言，南征受挫的深層影響在幾年後才顯現：523年破六鎮、523至530年間河北與關中的亂事、以及528年孝明帝被毒後隨即崩解的中央權威，使北魏再也無力組織規模相當的南征，江淮線反而在南北對峙中維持了數十年，直到北魏分裂為東魏、西魏，攻防重心才轉向中原內部。
impactEn: The significance of this fight does not lie in the number of casualties but in the fact that it marked the limit of Wei's southward advance. After the battle of Dunkou the lower Han remained a Chen defence zone and the Jingbei barrier below Xiangyang was never broken; it was not until 589, when the Sui army crossed the river and destroyed the Chen, that a northern dynasty wanting the middle Yangtze and the Jianghuai again had to push east along the same line of Xiangyang, Jiangxia and Jiankang. For more than nine hundred years after 567 that stretch of water was to be the dividing line between north and south, and the position Hou Zhen held at Dunkou was the very gate that the Sui army later had to break at greatest cost. For the Chen the price of the victory fell on a single man: with the death of their best field general the Xiangzhou military group was badly shaken, and Hou Zhen's son Hou Jing was later executed for arrogance and disorder, so that the group never again produced a man of Hou Zhen's standing, and the burden of the northern defence fell back on the court and the Jingzhou commanders; a few years later a collapse of the Hou Jing sort was staged again in the late Chen, with different actors. The deeper effect on the north became visible only a few years afterwards: the uprising of the Six Garrisons in 523, the disorder in Hebei and Guanzhong between 523 and 530, and the collapse of the central authority after Emperor Xiaoming was poisoned in 528, left Northern Wei without the strength to mount any campaign on the same scale, and the Jianghuai line held for decades instead, until Wei split into Eastern and Western Wei and the centre of gravity of the fighting moved inside the Central Plain.
result: 就567年這一天而言，結果是清楚的：北魏楊大眼所率的南征大軍在沌口被陳軍擊破，斬首數萬級，魏軍退回襄陽以北；陳朝守住了江夏、襄陽一線，侯瑱所部湘州兵完成了戰略上的反擊。陳軍之所以能在這一場佔上風，靠的不是兵力優勢——魏軍號稱二十萬，陳軍以湘州一區之兵應敵——而是地形選擇：把決戰地點放在漢水下游、放在弩的射程與水道縱深都能替自己服務的地方。魏軍的失敗也不是全因指揮失誤，楊大眼畢竟是經歷過鍾離之敗的老將，他一路攻克的節奏、進逼的速度都算得當，只是他把鍾離那次的水障教訓忘了，在陌生的江漢水網裡用上了在淮北平原奏效的打法。戰後的處理是雙方各得其所又各留隱憂：陳朝得到了一座可以守到隋朝的水上防線，代價是侯瑱這位宿將與他身後的湘州軍系就此崩散；北魏保住襄陽與河南，卻也明白江漢之水不可輕越，於是把重心轉回平定六鎮、鎮壓河北，而北魏的內亂正是在這一時期迅速坐大。此役之後三十餘年，北魏崩解，長江以北再成破碎局面，江漢防線反而成為南北分界的長線——沌口一戰的得失，就這樣被寫進了後來數百年的南北攻防史裡。
resultEn: For the day itself in 567 the result is clear: the invading army of Yang Dayan was broken at Dunkou by the Chen forces, tens of thousands of heads were taken, and the Wei fell back north of Xiangyang; the Chen held the line of Jiangxia and Xiangyang, and the Xiangzhou troops under Hou Zhen carried out a strategic counter-stroke. The Chen did not win on numbers, for the Wei are said to have numbered twenty myriads and the Chen answered with the troops of a single province, but on the choice of ground: the place of decision was put in the lower Han, where the range of the crossbow and the depth of the water both served the defender. The Wei defeat was not simply a fault of command; Yang Dayan was an old hand who had been checked at Zhongli and who kept a good pace and a sound tempo on the way in; what he forgot was the lesson of the water at Zhongli, and in the unfamiliar mesh of the Jianghan waterways he used the methods that had worked on the northern Huai plain. The aftermath suited each side and left each with a hidden cost. The Chen gained a waterborne defensive line that would hold until the Sui, and paid for it with the loss of Hou Zhen and the dispersal of the Xiangzhou military group. Wei kept Xiangyang and Henan, and learned in the same stroke that the waters of the Han could not be crossed lightly, so it turned its attention back to the Six Garrisons and to Hebei, where its own disorders grew rapidly. Within a little over thirty years the Northern Wei fell apart and the country north of the Yangtze broke into fragments, and the Jinghan line became instead the long line that divided north from south; the gains and losses of Dunkou were thus written into the several centuries of northern and southern campaigning that followed.
